discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators (the quantum spin Hall effect)
subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological phases of matter)
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can produce a new electronic phase protected by time-reversal symmetry, the quantum spin Hall insulator, and introduced the Z2 topological invariant that distinguishes it from ordinary insulators. With Fu, Kane extended this to three dimensions, predicting protected Dirac surface states. Molenkamp's group delivered the decisive experimental proof in 2007, observing quantised edge conduction in HgTe quantum wells. This work turned band topology from an abstract idea into a predictive materials principle: it launched the worldwide search for topological insulators, led to Bi2Se3-family materials, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, and Dirac and Weyl semimetals, and reshaped how electronic structure is classified through symmetry indicators and topological materials databases. It is a model of the chain from deep concept to quantitative prediction to laboratory verification, and its impact on condensed matter physics over two decades is of Nobel calibre.
